direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is a complete mess because they didn't know what bit to commit to, trying to shift the perspective from the killer to the main character, but then tossing in regular coverage along with following POVs of both the main character and Johnny, showing they couldn't commit to what type of movie they wanted to make and tried to appeal to everyone instead of the audience they already had; it feels like they are rehashing the bit from a different perspective in a worse way, and not a single kill is better than the first movie except for one bunk bed kill with the organs near the end that was on par; the direction on a microscale is terrible as it is the most generic, laughable, on-the-nose teens-at-a-sleepaway-camp bit with partying camp counselors, and the direction of the actors is atrocious, especially setting up a child actor to fail by not knowing how to direct children; the storytelling loses the gimmick entirely by putting it in the perspective of this main character, strictly copying the most formulaic sleepaway camp slasher template ever; the tension is supposed to be built on the anticipation of gory kills, but because you don't care about a single character or feel emotionally invested in them, you have zero reason to give a shit when they die

performance.comments: Completely stripped of the subtle physical presence and intrigue that made him compelling in the first film, reduced here to just another mindless, generic slasher villain who gives you zero reason to care

Set up to fail by atrocious character writing and abysmal direction that never should have put a child actor in this position, resulting in an unbearable, whiny screen presence that falls entirely on the director for not knowing how to guide young actors

cast.comments: An awful, painfully generic ensemble of teenage sleepaway camp stereotypes that proves why the first movie succeeded by hiding its performers behind a silent killer POV, completely exposing how bad the acting is when forced to deliver dialogue; a total failure from the writer for handing them such garbage material and from the director for having no idea how to direct this cast

story.comments: The concept is awful because it completely abandons the killer-POV gimmick that made the first film somewhat enjoyable and culturally relevant in the first place, turning into the most generic story imaginable about a bullied, nerdy kid at a sleepaway camp who summons Johnny to slaughter his bullies and hangs out with camp counselors, while lazily rehashing the lore from the original right where it left off; the plot structure copies the Friday the 13th summer camp slasher template to a T, dragging out the story endlessly just to pad the runtime with pointless filler; character writing is downright atrocious and some of the worst I have ever seen, giving us a whiny, completely unlikable main character who is impossible to empathize with, a bunch of generic horny camp counselor tropes, and an attempt to tease a traumatic-brain-injury hallucination twist that this movie simply does not deserve fan theories for, all while stripping Johnny of any of the subtle depth he had in the original and turning him into a totally hollow slasher

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is fucking atrocious, serving up the most generic, slasher-sequel-coded teen banter imaginable, and it boggles my mind why they chose to make this a dialogue-heavy film when the first movie succeeded precisely because they knew their limits and relied on the visual gimmick rather than writing ability; the humor tries way too hard with stereotypical teen slasher shock value, but because the characters are so insufferable, the only real laughs come from how laughably terrible the movie is; the symbolism is non-existent beyond half-baked hints that the entire thing might just be a traumatic-brain-injury hallucination or a dream sequence, but this movie does not deserve that level of fan theory generosity and offers absolutely nothing meaningful to chew on; the foreshadowing is blatantly obvious and right on the nose throughout, proving once again that these filmmakers had no idea how to construct an actual mystery or narrative

score.comments: There is no score just like the original, but while the ambient silence worked when following the killer, here the lack of music just makes the movie feel unbearably slow and hollow as you are forced to listen to agonizing walking and footsteps for 90 minutes

cinematography.comments: Fails completely because it refuses to commit to a visual bit, awkwardly alternating between third-person tracking shots of the victims, third-person tracking shots of Johnny, and traditional multi-angle coverage; instead of sticking strictly to the killer POV that fans liked or committing fully to a standard slasher format, it tries to do both to appeal to everyone and ends up pleasing nobody

editing.comments: Standard low-budget horror slasher editing that feels disjointed as it tries to cut together multiple shot perspectives and conflicting visual styles rather than the clean, singular focus of the original

sound.comments: Very generic low-budget horror audio that occasionally failed to sync or match up properly on screen, though to be fair that could partly be due to this screening being an unfinished festival work-in-progress cut

visual_effects.comments: Leans entirely into practical slasher effects that look noticeably cheap, with only one kill involving a bunk bed and exposed organs near the end coming close to the creative bar of the first movie

production_design.comments: Rehashes the exact same forest and cabin aesthetic from the first movie, blended with the most generic sleepaway summer camp layout imaginable

makeup.comments: Standard low-budget horror gore that looks cheap across the board despite how aggressively bloody they try to make every kill sequence

costumes.comments: Johnny's costume looks noticeably worse than it did in the original, coming across like a cheap Temu knockoff of his previous look

review.pacing: Unbearably slow as the constant scenes of slow walking and footsteps with zero score make the runtime feel endless; nothing genuinely happens for long stretches and they easily could have trimmed this down to 70 minutes, because this entire movie genuinely could have been an email
review.climax: Extremely poorly executed as the climax and ending desperately try to subvert expectations by playing into a tacky 'was it real or was it all in his head' ambiguous twist that falls completely flat
review.tone: Abandons the cold, singular atmosphere of the original in favor of the most tired, formulaic camp slasher tone imaginable, filled with drunk, horny teen counselors partying in the woods
review.final_notes: Saw the work-in-progress cut premiere at Fantastic Fest as a secret screening, but I don't think there is anything they could realistically change to save this movie
review.overall: Overall, 'In a Violent Nature: Part 2' is one of the worst movies I have ever seen at a film festival, abandoning the unique killer-POV gimmick that made the original work in favor of a hollow, formulaic teen slasher nobody asked for; weighed down by atrocious writing, nonexistent direction that sets up its young lead to fail, and agonizingly slow pacing where practically nothing happens, this is an entirely unnecessary sequel that has no business existing; while I did see a working cut print during the Fantastic Fest secret screening, I doubt there is anything they could change to save this trainwreck
